html:
The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was a truce signed in March 628 at Hudaybiyyah, just outside Mecca, between the prophet Muhammad and the quraysh leaders of the city.

Muhammad had marched with about 1,400 followers from Medina to make the pilgrimage to the Kaaba. The Quraysh would not let them in. After talks, both sides agreed to a ten year peace, and the Muslims would return home but could make the pilgrimage the following year. Some of the terms seemed to favour Mecca, and many Muslims were unhappy.

In practice the pact brought Muhammad recognition as an equal power and let Islam spread peacefully among the Arab tribes. When the Quraysh's allies broke the truce, Muhammad marched on the city in the conquest of Mecca in 630.
sum: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was a truce signed in March 628 at Hudaybiyyah, just outside Mecca, between the prophet Muhammad and the quraysh leaders of the city.
